title: WorldEnvironment tonemapping makes ViewportTexture colour incorrect
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.4.1 stable and 4.5 beta 3

### System information

Void #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Jun 21 02:19:00 UTC 2025 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970 (nvidia; 570.169) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600K CPU @ 3.80GHz (4 threads) - 15.50 GiB memory

### Issue description

I was trying to use SubViewports to make portals and noticed that regardless of which combination of settings I use in the material / shader or the SubViewport, the colour of the SubViewport's ViewportTexture is slightly off. I eventually figured it out and I guess there might be a use for it but by default if you use tonemapping other than linear with an exposure of 1.0 in the WorldEnvironment, the texture is the wrong colour because the tonemapping gets applied twice. Once for the SubViewport and then again in the root Viewport. This can be remedied by creating a new environment for the camera in the SubViewport with tonemapping set to the default settings. I think this should be stated somewhere in the documentation if it's not a bug because I feel like the use case for tonemapping a ViewportTexture must be rare.

### Steps to reproduce

- Set tonemapping in WorldEnvironment to something non-default (e.g. Filmic)
- Add SubViewport with camera and add ViewportTexture pointing to the SubViewport to a mesh
